'''Victor''' ('''Viktor''') '''Abramovich Zalgaller''' ({{langx|he|ויקטור אבּרמוביץ' זלגלר}}; {{langx|ru|Виктор Абрамович Залгаллер}}; 25 December 1920 &ndash; 2 October 2020) was a Russian-Israeli mathematician in the fields of [[geometry]] and [[Mathematical optimization|optimization]]. He is best known for the results he achieved on [[Polyhedron|convex polyhedra]], [[linear programming|linear]] and [[dynamic programming]], [[isoperimetry]], and [[differential geometry]].

==Biography==
Zalgaller was born in [[Parfino]], [[Novgorod Governorate]] on 25 December 1920.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.vestnik.com/issues/2001/0522/win/zalgaller.htm|title=Виктор Залгаллер (Израиль)|website=Vestnik|access-date=3 October 2020|language=ru}}</ref> In 1936, he was one of the winners of the Leningrad Mathematics Olympiads for high school students. He started his studies at the [[Saint Petersburg State University|Leningrad State University]], however, [[World War II]] intervened in 1941, and Zalgaller joined the [[Red Army]]. He took part in the defence of [[Leningrad]], and in 1945 marched into Germany.<ref name="weismann">{{cite web|url=https://wis-wander.weizmann.ac.il/math-computer-science/life-begins-80|title=Life Begins at 80|website=Weizmann Institute of Science|date=27 September 2012|access-date=3 October 2020}}</ref>

He worked as a teacher at the [[Saint Petersburg Lyceum 239]],<ref name="ru239"/> and received his 1963<ref name="math">{{cite web|url=https://mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=79075|title=Victor Abramovich Zalgaller|website=Math Genealogy|access-date=3 October 2020}}</ref> doctoral dissertation on polyhedra with the aid of his high school students who wrote the computer programs for the calculation.<ref name="ru239"/>

Zalgaller did his early work under direction of [[Aleksandr Aleksandrov (mathematician)|Aleksandr Aleksandrov]] and [[Leonid Kantorovich]].  He wrote joint [[monograph]]s with both of them.  His later monograph ''Geometric Inequalities'' (joint with [[Yuri Burago]]) is still the main reference in the field.

Zalgaller lived in [[Saint Petersburg]] most of his life, having studied and worked at the [[Saint Petersburg State University|Leningrad State University]] and the [[Steklov Institute of Mathematics]] (Saint Petersburg branch).

In 1999, he immigrated to [[Israel]]. Zalgaller died on 2 October 2020 at the age of 99.<ref name="ru239">{{cite web|url=http://www.239.ru/mainnews/skonchalsya-vazalgaller-0|title=Скончался В.А.Залгаллер|website=[[Saint Petersburg Lyceum 239]]|access-date=3 October 2020|language=ru|archive-date=26 November 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201126154145/https://www.239.ru/mainnews/skonchalsya-vazalgaller-0|url-status=dead}}</ref>
